suggestionRules.rule: Always use explicit TypeScript return types and avoid the 'any' type.
Prefer functional programming principles such as pure functions and immutability.
Use Next.js App Router with server components by default. Add 'use client' only when necessary.
Use async/await syntax for asynchronous logic. Avoid .then() chains.
Do not directly mutate req or res in Next.js route handlers.
Use Tailwind CSS utility classes only. Avoid custom CSS unless absolutely necessary.
Use Tailwind responsive prefixes like 'md:', 'lg:' and 'dark:' for adaptive design.
Use 'clsx' or 'classnames' for managing conditional class names.
Use Prisma Client with fully typed queries. Avoid raw SQL.
Always wrap Prisma queries in try/catch when used in API or Server Actions.
Keep Prisma schema logic clean. Do not write business logic in migration or schema files.
Separate data logic into services or repositories, not in pages or routes.
Use kebab-case for folder and file naming. Keep naming consistent across the codebase.
Organize files by feature (feature-first structure), not by file type.
Place reusable components in a /components or /ui directory with clear, self-descriptive names.
Validate all user inputs on the server side using Zod or similar schema validators.
Escape user-generated content when rendering HTML to prevent XSS.
Never hardcode secrets or environment values. Use environment variables and .env files.
Keep components modular and under 100 lines if possible. Break into subcomponents when needed.
Avoid unnecessary re-renders. Use useMemo, useCallback, and memoization appropriately.
